trajectory_summary: This is a short, mechanically-run call that starts rocky — a confused customer, an audio/connectivity hiccup on the rep's side, and a very late self-introduction — but recovers into a cooperative, completed booking. The rep never builds emotional engagement or flips the bill pain into a reason to act, but procedurally the call lands: bill photo captured, appointment day/time locked, spouse-on-title flagged but not addressed.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday) and time (11:00) are locked for a phone appointment, with the customer confirming her own schedule allows it; however, the husband identified as a co-owner at 00:48 is never confirmed as part of the appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures a rough bill figure but immediately moves to the roof question without clarifying the number or ever referencing it again as the reason to book or care about the appointment; the flip should have landed around 05:36 when locking the appointment time, tying the bill pain to what the specialist call will address.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks a version of 'what interested you in solar' — the call moves directly from intro into address/co-owner/utility/bill/roof/credit verify questions without ever surfacing the customer's motivation.

primary_coaching_focus.why: A co-owner was identified on title early in the call but never invited onto the Monday 11:00 appointment — per protocols.spouse_decision this is a structural booking risk, not just a missed nicety, since the closer may find the actual decision-maker absent.

key_moments.stewart_read: The customer identifies a co-owner (husband) on the title, which per protocol should trigger the rep to plan to include him on the appointment call. The rep never circles back to this — no mention of the husband when scheduling the phone appointment for Monday at 11:00.

The customer gives an unclear, unconfirmed bill figure ('4 something, 5 something') and the rep moves straight to the next verify item without clarifying the number or later using it to build urgency.

This answer to 'what utility company are you with?' doesn't make sense as a company name — likely a transcription/audio garble — yet the rep accepts it without clarifying, the same low-quality-capture pattern seen with the bill amount at 01:04. Later in the call the rep independently names 'Eversource' as the utility, suggesting the rep had the correct answer from elsewhere (form data) rather than from this exchange.
